presentingComplaint: 3 days of high fever with rigors, breathlessness and confusion, brought in obtunded and hypotensive
history: Previously healthy labourer with ongoing intravenous heroin use for several years, injecting into groin veins. Over 3 days he developed abrupt high fever, drenching sweats and rapidly worsening exertional then rest breathlessness with orthopnoea. On the morning of admission relatives found him drowsy and confused with slurred speech and a drooping right face, prompting emergency transfer. No prior known valve disease, no dental work. This is a fulminant, acute course rather than the classic weeks-long low-grade subacute illness.
examination: Toxic, diaphoretic and peripherally shut down. Confused (GCS 13, E3V4M6) with a dense right facial droop and right arm drift suggesting an embolic event. Mottled cool peripheries, capillary refill 4s. Loud new early-diastolic murmur at the left sternal edge with a wide pulse pressure and bounding then thready pulses; bibasal crepitations to mid-zones. A few non-blanching lesions on the pulps of fingers and a small painless macule on the right sole. Fresh and healed needle-track marks over both groins.
imaging: Portable CXR: bilateral alveolar interstitial oedema consistent with acute pulmonary oedema from acute aortic regurgitation, no cavitating septic emboli. Non-contrast CT head: early hypodensity in left MCA territory in keeping with septic embolic infarct, no haemorrhage. Transthoracic then transoesophageal echo: large (14 mm) mobile vegetation on the aortic valve with a leaflet perforation and severe acute aortic regurgitation; hyperdynamic LV, no abscess seen but aortic root oedematous.
microbiology: Three sets of blood cultures drawn from separate sites all flag positive within 12 hours for Gram-positive cocci in clusters; speciated as Staphylococcus aureus, methicillin-resistant (MRSA) on rapid PBP2a/PCR. Repeat cultures at 48h remain positive (persistent bacteraemia).
differentialDiagnoses: Infective endocarditis (acute, native aortic valve, MRSA)
Vascular catheter / injection-site device-type deep infection
Embolic ischaemic stroke of cardiac origin
finalDiagnosis: Acute MRSA native aortic-valve infective endocarditis complicated by severe acute aortic regurgitation, cardiogenic/septic shock and septic cerebral embolism (Modified Duke: definite — 2 major: typical organism with persistent bacteraemia + echo vegetation with new regurgitation)
citations: ESC — Guidelines for the Management of Infective Endocarditis — 2023
AHA — Infective Endocarditis in Adults: Diagnosis, Antimicrobial Therapy, and Management of Complications — 2015
stewardship: Severe, culture-positive MRSA native-valve endocarditis with shock: after 2-3 sets of blood cultures, start empiric IV vancomycin (targeting AUC/MIC) plus gentamicin pending sensitivities; de-escalate to targeted anti-staphylococcal therapy per susceptibilities. Urgent cardiac surgery referral for valve replacement given severe acute AR with heart failure, large mobile vegetation, embolisation and persistent bacteraemia. Vancomycin is a protected/reserve agent — narrow once MSSA/MRSA status and MIC confirmed.
contraindications: Avoid aminoglycoside if worsening AKI — weigh nephrotoxicity against synergy benefit
Avoid delaying surgery for prolonged antibiotic course when acute severe AR causes refractory heart failure
Beta-lactam allergy history alters MSSA options if organism later methicillin-susceptible
edgeCases: MRSA vegetation may seed metastatic foci — screen for splenic/renal emboli and spinal/epidural abscess
Systemic embolism with cerebral infarct raises haemorrhagic transformation risk, complicating anticoagulation and surgical timing
Right-sided involvement can coexist in IVDU — assess tricuspid valve and for septic pulmonary emboli
expectedMaiK: An acutely toxic injection-drug user with a new early-diastolic (aortic regurgitant) murmur, embolic phenomena and persistent S. aureus bacteraemia has infective endocarditis until proven otherwise; obtain urgent echocardiography and blood cultures and involve cardiac surgery early.
expectedNextQuestions: Duration and pattern of fever and any prior similar episodes
Injection drug use details, sites and shared equipment
Any preceding dental/skin/soft-tissue infection or indwelling lines
Symptoms of embolisation — focal weakness, limb ischaemia, flank/abdominal pain
Prior valve disease, prosthetic material or cardiac devices
expectedInvestigations: Three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures before antibiotics
Serial lactate, renal function, CRP/procalcitonin and full blood count
CT head/whole-body imaging for embolic and metastatic foci
ECG to detect PR prolongation suggesting perivalvular/root abscess
regressionAssertions: New regurgitant murmur plus persistent S. aureus bacteraemia plus echo vegetation should satisfy definite endocarditis and not be triaged as undifferentiated sepsis alone
Empiric regimen must include MRSA cover (vancomycin) given severe presentation and injection drug use
Case must trigger urgent echocardiography and cardiac surgery referral for acute severe aortic regurgitation with shock
